title: What to watch at the open
text: Yesterday was one of the worst days in over a year. The S&P 500 fund SPY fell 4.4% to $733.00, and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ fell 6.5%. All 17 names on the list closed lower. The big event today is the October jobs report at 8:30 a.m. New York time, which shows how many people were hired last month. Watch whether prices keep falling, steady out, or bounce when trading opens at 9:30. Nobody can know which one in advance.

title: AI chip and equipment makers fell the most
text: The four big AI companies (Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta) fell about 3% on average. The five companies that sell parts and equipment for AI (NVIDIA, Broadcom, TSMC, Vertiv, AMD) fell about 12% on average. AMD dropped 17.3% and Vertiv 14.0%. Companies that sell the parts tend to swing more than the companies that use them.

title: Rates may stay high
text: The Fed held rates steady on October 28, but two members voted to raise them. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, up from about 4.06% a year earlier. The 10 year Treasury yield is what the government pays to borrow for 10 years. When it is high, safe bonds look better and fast growing tech stocks can look less attractive.

title: Analyst targets sit far above prices
text: A price target is where an analyst guesses a stock could trade in about a year. The average target for NVIDIA is $339.17 against a $181.60 close, and for AMD it is $645.82 against $404.40. Careful: targets update slowly, so many were set before the drop. A big gap is a clue to study, never a promise.

title: Lesson 40: What is the jobs report?
text: Once a month, the US government counts how many people got new jobs. That count is the jobs report. It also shows the unemployment rate, which is the share of people who want a job but do not have one. Why does a stock market care? A strong report means the economy is running hot, which can push the Fed to keep interest rates high. A weak report can worry people about companies earning less. Sometimes good news for workers makes stocks fall, because investors fear higher rates. The takeaway: the market often reacts to what the report means for interest rates, not only to the number itself.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices come from the November 5 market close. Analyst targets and ratios are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE only. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have price data but no targets or ratios. News reasons come from reports we could not all verify. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
